rows.label: Don't hand your agents the keys.
rows.text: An agent under Oxagen has its own identity and a mandate. For mediated connections, it does not receive a token to GitHub or a password to the database. When a task needs one of those systems, the agent asks. The request carries who started the task, which agent is asking, which tool it wants, and which data it would reach.

rows.label: A rule you wrote answers.
rows.text: The team that owns the system writes the rule. Reads of the public repo: allowed. A push to main: denied. A push to a release branch: routed to the release owner, who sees the request with the diff beside it and answers from the Access page. Allowed and denied requests settle inside the same call. Routed requests wait for the person, and the run waits with them.

rows.label: For mediated connections, the credential stays in Oxagen.
rows.text: Oxagen holds the credential and makes the connection on the agent's behalf when a rule allows the request. The agent does not receive the credential. The record shows each use: the request, the rule that answered it, and the person who signed it.

entries.title: Launch announcement
entries.long:
An agent workforce needs operators who can decide what each agent may do, equip it for the work, and inspect what happens. That job is workforce management, and Oxagen is where it happens.

Give each agent an identity. Set its authority and budget, assign tools and skills, and review requests that need a person's decision. The record connects governed actions to the agent, the rule, and the person responsible.

Some work has a finish line. Define its completion criteria before the agent starts and review the recorded results afterward. Other work continues. Keep its authority, activity, and spend in view as it runs.

Explore Oxagen to follow an agent from its assigned mandate to a recorded action.
entries.evidence: Product owner: provide a launch walkthrough with identity, authority, tool and skill assignment, a recorded action, an ongoing agent, and a task with completion criteria. Document supported environments and control boundaries. Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.

entries.title: One mandate, four clauses
entries.long: Identity systems say who the agent is. Gateways say which tools it can call. Billing says what it consumed. Prompt repositories say what it was told. Oxagen binds those into one mandate per agent, checks it on the actions routed through Oxagen, and keeps a record another person can read.

entries.title: The demo, in order
entries.long: Show an agent's identity and the mandate it works under. Let it request a push to a protected branch and get denied, with the rule id. Let it request a push to a release branch and watch the request route to a person, answer it from the Access page, and see the run resume. Open the run and show the request beside the tool call with its cost. Then show an ongoing agent with its budget and open requests, and a bounded task with its completion checks.

entries.notes: Run it on a prepared workspace. Do not promise it on a prospect's repositories without agreed setup.

entries.title: Write one rule for each thing an agent may ask for.
entries.long: A rule names a capability, a condition, and one of three effects: allow, deny, or require approval. For requests routed through Oxagen, requests that match allow or deny settle inside the call and leave a row with the rule id. Requests that match require approval wait for the person the rule names, and the run waits with them. Rules are checked after identity, so a rule can narrow what an agent may do and cannot widen it. In observe mode, the decision is recorded, not enforced.
entries.qualifier: For requests routed through Oxagen. Observe mode is recorded, not enforced.

entries.title: Define done before the work starts.
entries.short: For a bounded task, lock the required checks before the first tool call. The agent can read its definition of done without rewriting the terms.
entries.long: Describe the task and let Oxagen draft its definition of done, or supply your own for work that repeats. Specify the commands that must pass, the files that must be present, the paths a change may touch, and any human review required. Oxagen locks the criteria before the agent starts using tools.
entries.qualifier: For bounded tasks.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 17.

entries.title: Keep your judgment in the definition of done.
entries.short: Mechanical checks can hold while a run waits for a named reviewer. Pending stays visible until the decision is recorded.
entries.long: Some requirements need a person: whether a change matches the intent, whether the wording is right, whether the result is ready to use. Include that review in the definition of done. Oxagen keeps the verdict pending after mechanical checks hold until the required human decision arrives.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 19.

entries.title: The agent doesn't get to decide it's done.
entries.short: When the agent tries to stop, Oxagen runs the checks. A broken check sends it back with a specific reason.
entries.long: The agent reaches a stopping point. The wrapper runs the locked checks where the agent works. If they break and retries remain, it blocks the stop and returns the failing check IDs so the agent can continue. If retries run out, the run ends broken with its reasons recorded. Done means the specified checks held, and your team decides whether those checks are enough.
entries.qualifier: For bounded tasks with a definition of done.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 18. Bounded-task section only. Never a lead, a hero, an ad headline, or an email subject.

entries.title: Passing verdict
entries.long: A passing verdict means the specified checks held. Your team decides whether those checks are sufficient for the task. When checks fail, the record shows the reasons and whether the agent continued, waited for a person, or reached its retry limit.

entries.title: Check the verdict from the evidence.
entries.short: The recorded checks determine whether the definition of done held. The same evidence produces the same verdict.
entries.long: Oxagen settles the definition of done with a deterministic decision function. A model can draft the criteria, but it cannot choose the verdict. Review the locked criteria, the check results, and any outstanding human decisions to see exactly why the run is held, pending, or broken. A held verdict means the specified checks held, not that every requirement was captured.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 20.

entries.title: Give each agent an identity you can govern.
entries.short: Register each agent as a principal in a supported identity system, with its own roles, scope, and accountable operator.
entries.long: Each agent has a named place in your identity and access management system. Assign its roles, limit the resources it can request, and keep delegated authority within the operator's own permissions. Review its activity under that identity, and suspend or revoke its authority when its responsibility changes.

entries.short: Review who changed an agent's authority, approved a request, or adjusted its budget alongside the work that followed.
entries.long: Operating an agent workforce includes the decisions people make about it. Oxagen records governed administrative actions as well as agent activity. Follow a role change, approval, budget adjustment, or revocation to the responsible identity and supporting record. Give reviewers the history behind the current settings.

entries.title: Set the terms for work that keeps going.
entries.short: Manage an ongoing responsibility through authority, budgets, rules, and human review. Define done when the task calls for it.
entries.long: Some assignments end with a deliverable. Others continue across many runs. Set the agent's permitted actions, spending limits, tools, and approval rules for the responsibility it holds. Inspect individual runs and intervene when needed. Apply a definition of done to bounded tasks within that work without pretending the whole responsibility is finished.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.

entries.title: Choose the procedures your agents can use.
entries.short: Manage skills, approve what agents can find and load, and see which skills reached the work.
entries.long: A skill captures a procedure your agents can follow. Oxagen governs which skills are in scope and how much context they may consume. Review configuration changes through pull requests and inspect what each run loaded, what was withheld, and why. The agent's harness carries out the procedure.
entries.evidence: Engineering owner: show how an operator changes an assignment, which version an agent receives, and when the change takes effect. Do not promise centralized revocation or version pinning without demonstrated behavior.

entries.short: Manage the tool catalog and control which tools each agent can discover and request.
entries.long: Equip agents for their responsibilities from a governed tool catalog. Set access by role and scope, then inspect the toolbelt the agent actually sees. Each request still meets your rules before the action proceeds. A tool's presence in the catalog does not grant every agent permission to use it.
entries.evidence: Engineering owner: show how an operator changes an assignment, which version an agent receives, and when the change takes effect. Do not promise centralized revocation or version pinning without demonstrated behavior.

When an allowed request uses a mediated connection, Oxagen uses the connection credential on the agent's behalf, and the agent does not receive it. You can read what the agent requested, which rule answered, and who signed an approval.

entries.long: Set the budget where accountability sits. Oxagen checks hard budgets before model calls through its proxy and applies supported controls through the wrapper. A budget-triggered pause appears in the run with its reason, so the operator can decide whether to fund more work or stop there.

Code, business knowledge, and reviewed lessons can reach the agent alongside the task. The run records what was supplied and where it came from, so you can inspect the information behind a decision.

Each finding links to the recorded calls behind it and the cost they added, so you can choose what to fix first.

entries.title: Your agents. Their work. One place to act.
entries.short: See what each enrolled agent is doing, what it needs, and what it costs. Answer, steer, fund, or stop it from one console.
entries.long: An agent waiting for approval. Another nearing its budget. A third working from the wrong assumption. Oxagen brings their runs, requests, mandates, and spend into one view. Open the run, read what happened, and take the next action with the record beside you.
entries.qualifier: Agents enrolled in Oxagen, with the controls each integration supports.
entries.evidence: Product owner: provide a launch walkthrough with identity, authority, tool and skill assignment, a recorded action, an ongoing agent, and a task with completion criteria. Document supported environments and control boundaries. Platform owner: demonstrate allow, deny, approval, missing-rule, observe-mode, and outage cases for each supported integration. Identify requests outside that boundary.
entries.notes: Launch card 1.

entries.title: Try another path from the moment that mattered.
entries.short: Fork a supported recording with its captured context and tool responses to explore how a different decision changes the work.
entries.long: Start from a recorded point instead of reconstructing the run by hand. Oxagen supplies the captured context and recorded tool responses while the model makes a fresh call. Compare the resulting runs to see where they diverge. A failure becomes a concrete case you can investigate again.
entries.evidence: Product owner: demonstrate a fork from a supported recording with captured context and recorded tool responses.
entries.notes: Launch card 12.

entries.title: Put the decision in the right hands.
entries.short: Route the requests that need judgment to the people responsible, with the action and its context ready to review.
entries.long: Your rules decide when a person needs to look. Oxagen pauses the governed request and shows the reviewer which agent asked, what it wants to do, and the authority it would use. The run resumes with the answer recorded. Routine requests can proceed under the rules you already set.
entries.evidence: Platform owner: demonstrate allow, deny, approval, missing-rule, observe-mode, and outage cases for each supported integration. Identify requests outside that boundary.
entries.notes: Launch card 4.

entries.title: Change course while the work is happening.
entries.short: Add a constraint, correct an assumption, or redirect a live run. See when your instruction reaches the agent.
entries.long: Open a run and send the correction where it matters. Deliver steering after the current step, at the next turn, or by interrupting where the connection supports it. Oxagen records the instruction and its delivery status, so you can tell whether it is still waiting or has entered the agent's context.
entries.qualifier: Interrupts where the connection supports them.
entries.evidence: Product owner: demonstrate delivery after the current step, at the next turn, and by interrupt, for each supported connection.
entries.notes: Launch card 5.

entries.title: Set the terms your agents work under.
entries.short: Set access, budget, rules, tools, and steering in one mandate, whichever team owns each part.
entries.long: A mandate is the one object an agent works under. It names what the agent may request, what it may spend, and which tools and instructions it may use. Oxagen checks those terms on governed calls and records the decision, so the people setting the limits can see how they were applied.
entries.qualifier: Checked on governed calls.
entries.evidence: Platform owner: demonstrate allow, deny, approval, missing-rule, observe-mode, and outage cases for each supported integration. Identify requests outside that boundary.
entries.notes: Launch card 2. The launch card named security, FinOps, and engineering as the owners. The copy no longer requires a particular org chart.

entries.title: Stop the next action at the boundary.
entries.short: Pause a run or revoke authority for an agent, a tool, or a workspace. Oxagen records what the control stopped.
entries.long: When a run needs attention, pause it at the next supported boundary. When authority needs to end, revoke it at the scope that fits: one agent, one connection, a class of tools, or the organization. Governed calls meet the new restriction before proceeding, and the affected runs show the reason.
entries.qualifier: At the next supported boundary, for governed calls.
entries.evidence: Platform owner: demonstrate allow, deny, approval, missing-rule, observe-mode, and outage cases for each supported integration. Identify requests outside that boundary.
entries.notes: Launch card 6.

entries.title: Match the bill to the record.
entries.short: Reconcile recorded spend with provider usage and invoices. Open a difference and see the unmatched entries.
entries.long: Oxagen matches provider charges to recorded calls where request identifiers are available, then to usage totals and invoice lines. Differences become visible exceptions with the records attached. You can see how much spend is matched, what remains unresolved, and where the numbers diverge.
entries.evidence: Finance owner: show a sample cost row, rate source, attribution fields, exclusions, and reconciliation to billed totals. Use an explicit comparison set before making comparative claims.
entries.notes: Launch card 9.

entries.title: Turn a lesson from one run into steering for the next.
entries.short: Capture what agents learn, review the supporting evidence, and publish new steering through a pull request.
entries.long: A useful discovery should survive the run that made it. Oxagen links learned records to the work behind them and proposes changes to shared steering. Your team reviews the proposal in its own repository. Merge publishes the change, giving future runs the lesson and your team a versioned history of what went into force.
entries.cta: Follow a lesson into the next run
entries.evidence: Engineering owner: follow one learned record to a reviewed pull request and to a later run that received the steering.
entries.notes: Launch card 14. The launch card title said a rule for the next run. A rule answers requests, and a lesson becomes steering.

entries.title: See what a rule would change before it does.
entries.short: Test a proposed rule against your agents' recorded calls before putting it into force.
entries.long: A tighter rule can stop the wrong action and interrupt useful work. Oxagen shows how a proposed version would have answered real requests: which would be denied, which would need approval, and which would become allowed. Review those differences before activating the change.
entries.evidence: Platform owner: replay a proposed rule against recorded calls and show the denied, routed, and newly allowed differences.
entries.notes: Launch card 13.

entries.title: See what the agent saw.
entries.short: Step through a recorded run with its instructions, tool results, decisions, and accumulated cost in view.
entries.long: Scrub to the moment a run changed direction. Where the recording retains full content, you can read the context the agent received, what it asked, what came back, and what it had spent by then. Playback skips long waits while preserving the real elapsed time. Each run shows the playback capabilities its evidence supports.
entries.qualifier: Where the recording retains full content.
entries.evidence: Product owner: show which runs retain full content and which playback capabilities each run's evidence supports.
entries.notes: Launch card 11.

entries.title: Share the evidence with the answer.
entries.short: Export a signed run record with its actions, decisions, costs, and evidence for independent inspection.
entries.long: Oxagen links recorded frames in a hash chain and signs the run's close. An exported record lets a reviewer check its integrity outside the product. It identifies what the gateway observed, what the agent's wrapper reported, and where evidence is missing, so the strength of the record stays visible.
entries.evidence: Security owner: export a signed run record and check its integrity outside the product, including where evidence is missing.
entries.notes: Launch card 16. The title no longer says hand over, which the kit keeps for the line about the keys.

entries.title: Read your AI bill down to the work.
entries.short: Follow spend from the organization to the operator, agent, run, and individual call that incurred it.
entries.long: Open a spend total and keep going until you reach the work behind it. Oxagen records model usage by token class, the rate applied, and the agent and operator responsible. Finance and engineering read the same underlying records, with measured, reported, and estimated costs identified.
entries.evidence: Finance owner: show a sample cost row, rate source, attribution fields, exclusions, and reconciliation to billed totals. Use an explicit comparison set before making comparative claims.
entries.notes: Launch card 7.

entries.title: Your agents get a mandate. Your operators get a review.
entries.short: See who spent the AI budget, and what it bought.
entries.long:
One page per person, read from the record and not estimated. It shows what that operator spent, broken out by agent and by workspace, and what the spend bought: for bounded tasks, the outcome beside the dollars.

It also shows how the person works with their agents, taken from the recorded turns. Turns to completion. Restarts on the same task. Steering overridden by hand instead of written as a rule. Routed requests the operator approved every time. Each habit carries its definition, so the reader can check the number against the rows it came from.

Each habit comes with one recommendation, worded as a rule the operator can adopt. The review reports what the record shows. It does not grade the person: twelve restarts on the same task this week is a fact, and bad prompter is not one.
entries.cta_destination: One operator's review, showing spend by agent and workspace read from the same rows the Spend page prices, one prompt habit with its definition, and the rule the review recommends.
entries.qualifier: The review reads the recorded turns and governed actions Oxagen holds for that operator.
entries.evidence: Product owner: demonstrate a per-operator spend row read from the same rows the Spend page prices, one prompt-habit metric with its written definition and the turns behind it, and the rule the review recommends for that habit. Finance owner: reconcile the per-operator total to the billed total and name the exclusions. Do not present a habit as a rating of the person or claim a saving without the measured workload.
entries.notes: The entry point for the rate job, and the human half of the AI bill. Held until the operator review ships. The habits are facts from the record with their definitions beside them, never a score.

entries.title: Product page introduction
entries.long: Oxagen is workforce management for the operators running an agent workforce. Register agents with their own identities, assign roles and authority, and choose the tools, skills, and knowledge they can use. Set budgets, direct live work, and review requests that need your judgment. For work with a finish line, define what done means and how it will be checked. For ongoing responsibilities, set the operating limits and review the record. Oxagen brings the authority, activity, cost, and evidence for governed work together in one agent control plane.
entries.evidence: Product owner: provide a launch walkthrough with identity, authority, tool and skill assignment, a recorded action, an ongoing agent, and a task with completion criteria. Document supported environments and control boundaries.
entries.notes: Adapted from the recommended lead in the launch cards. Its title is not a second headline: the hero headline leads.

entries.title: Short pitch
entries.long: Your operators decide what each agent is responsible for, what it may do, and what it needs to work. Oxagen gives those decisions a home: an agent identity, a mandate for authority and budget, assigned tools and skills, and a record of governed activity. For bounded work, define completion before it starts. For ongoing work, manage the agent's authority, requests, and spend as it operates.

entries.title: The buyer's pain stays internal.
entries.long: What this buyer says in a room is qualification material, not copy. A large invoice for a small change, a review that cannot name the agent or explain why it took the path it took, and pressure from above for output the reporting cannot substantiate: all three belong in discovery notes and in the positioning reference, and none of them belongs in a headline, an ad, a subject line, or a slide. Published copy states the mechanism and lets the reader draw the comparison. Do not sell the fear, do not describe the prospect's setup back to them, and do not argue with what their provider reports. See rule-outreach, rule-no-competitors, and finding 06.

entries.title: Completion is a control for bounded tasks.
entries.long: The definition of done applies to work with an endpoint. Ongoing responsibilities are managed through authority, budget, and review points. A passing verdict means the specified checks held, and the team decides whether those checks suffice.

entries.title: Show cost. Claim savings only from a measurement.
entries.long: Cost visibility is a launch claim. A saving is stated only for a measured workload under stated conditions, with the baseline named. Make no comparison with model providers.

entries.title: Scope every enforcement claim.
entries.long: Say for actions routed through Oxagen, or governed calls. Observe mode is recorded, not enforced. A workspace with no rules answers requests by identity alone.

entries.title: First contact uses run, request, rule, check, and cost.
entries.long: Define mandate once, beside the task. Frames, seals, and witness verdicts belong in detail pages and docs, with their definitions. Familiar explanatory words may sit around exact UI labels.

entries.title: Held entries wait for their gate.
entries.long: An entry with release held stays out of the site, ads, and outreach until every capability in its gate ships. Using it early claims what the record cannot yet show.

entries.title: Sell to the executive accountable for the agent workforce.
entries.long: The operator is the user. The buyer is the technology executive who answers for the agent workforce and its spend, usually a CIO or a CTO, and who is asked to ship autonomous agents across the company while a modernization program is already in flight. They can see the total. They cannot yet say which agent spent it, on whose behalf, or under which rule. What they buy is the ability to answer: an identity per agent, a mandate a named team wrote, and a record of governed activity another person can read. Qualify on five signals: agents running in more than one team with no single page that lists them, a named person accountable for agent spend who cannot attribute it below the account, a migration or modernization program in flight, security and finance and engineering each writing their part of an agent somewhere different, and a request from above for output the current reporting cannot substantiate. Skip, for now: one team with one agent, agents that only read, no one accountable for the spend, and a mandate to stop agent adoption rather than to operate it. Open with a diagnostic question, not with an assertion about their setup. See rule-outreach.
entries.notes: This entry names who signs, not who the product speaks to on the homepage. The operator stays the primary user audience and the reader of most copy. The full statement, the qualifying and disqualifying signals, and the opening questions are in skills/oxagen-branding/references/positioning.md under The buyer we are built for.

entries.title: Identity and credentials are separate claims.
entries.long: Each agent has its own identity. For mediated connections, Oxagen uses the connection credential on the agent's behalf and the agent does not receive it. Make no promise about what an agent cannot leak.
phrases: nothing for the agent to leak

entries.title: Business context stays inside permitted scope.
entries.long: Give agents the business context their work requires, within the scope each agent is permitted to read. Make no claim of universal recall or of every agent sharing everything.
phrases: every agent you run has it

entries.title: Lead with the clause the reader owns.
entries.long: A security lead reads access first. A finance lead reads budget first. An engineering lead reads equipment first, then the record. One person may own all four.

entries.title: Workforce management for autonomous agents is the product. The agent control plane is the category.
entries.long: Lead with workforce management for autonomous agents, the job the operator is doing. Name the technical category the agent control plane, for an architecture review, a platform owner's evaluation, or a docs overview. Mission Control is retired as of 2026-09-19, because GitHub's control-plane product carries that name, and it never appears in live copy. Where copy needs to name the place an operator works, say Oxagen or the operator console, lowercase and descriptive. Fleet is the name of the Fleet page and an operator's word for the agents they run, not a category. Workforce is the population of agents. Operator is the person. Autonomous agents is allowed in the category line and in body copy as a plain description of what Oxagen manages, and the headline names the workforce rather than narrowing the claim, because Oxagen governs supervised agents too.
entries.notes: Retired entries and the before half of a voice pair are exempt from the phrase check, so the retired lines can still be quoted where they are named as retired.

entries.title: No AI-powered verification.
entries.long: The verdict has no model in it. That is the point.

entries.title: Auto-approve is not a feature.
entries.long: A rule that allows is a decision someone wrote down. Say allowed by rule.

entries.title: Never name a competitor.
entries.long: Describe the category behavior instead: tools that record, a token with everything the agent might ever need, scores written after the fact, a second model grading the first. The reader supplies the names.

entries.title: Do not hand over the keys in the copy.
entries.long: Connect your agent to, give the agent access to, and the agent's API key each hand over the keys in the copy even where the product does not.

entries.title: Do not name a category someone else owns.
entries.long: Not observability, governance as a category, evals, guardrails, or a trust layer. Each is owned, and each means watch and report. Name the category by what it does.

entries.title: Ask. Do not assert the prospect's setup.
entries.long: Outreach opens with a diagnostic question. Buyer statements are labelled hypothetical. Traction numbers, partner counts, and setup durations stay out of copy until an owner supplies dated evidence and publication approval.

entries.title: No prospect names, deal details, or investor figures.
entries.long: This repository is public. Keep prospects, deals, and investor figures in outreach tools. The check fails on the markers listed in this file, and on the names in the untracked local file messages/rules/prospect-names.local.txt, which never enters git because a blocklist of names would publish them.

entries.title: Proven sits beside a witness flip and its scope.
entries.long: Use proven only where a witness flipped, and say which requirement it covers. A held dod is done, not proven.

entries.title: The registry is the source of truth.
entries.long: Every published line starts as an entry in messages/. The message bank, the index, and the ads are generated from it. Nothing keeps a hand count of lines.

entries.title: State SOC 2 status only from the report.
entries.long: State an actual completed examination, report type, covered entity and system, examination period or date, and report access process only when supported by the report. If the launch status is readiness work or support for customer controls, describe that specific status and scope. Do not turn auditable, or an ambition, into an attestation claim. No report has been inspected for this registry, so no entry makes a SOC 2 claim.

entries.title: Follow the action back to its authority.
entries.long: Review which agent requested an action, on whose behalf, which rule answered, and who approved it when a person was required. Inspect the recorded result and cost alongside that decision. For runs with completion checks, export the record so another person can recompute the recorded verdict without an Oxagen account or network connection.
entries.qualifier: An exported verdict does not establish that every requirement was captured or that every action was correct.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Auditability describes the evidence available for review. Use proven only beside a defined witness result and its scope.

entries.title: Set the authority behind each action.
entries.long: Give each agent its own identity in your identity and access management system. Set which actions it may request and which resources it may reach. For actions handled through Oxagen, rules allow the request, deny it, or route it to a person. The record connects the decision to the agent and the person responsible for its work.
entries.qualifier: For actions handled through Oxagen.
entries.evidence: Platform owner: demonstrate allow, deny, approval, missing-rule, observe-mode, and outage cases for each supported integration. Identify requests outside that boundary. Security owner: demonstrate provisioning, delegation, revocation, credential handling, and audit coverage. Before an attestation claim, verify the report type, entity, system scope, period, and access process against the actual report.
entries.notes: Detail page: name the supported identity systems and explain provisioning, delegation, revocation, and enforcement boundaries. IAM identity must describe the implemented relationship, not only an internal agent ID.

entries.title: Manage the agents. Coach the operators.
entries.long: The mandate sets what an agent may do. The review shows how the person working with it spends the budget and how they ask. Read the spend by operator, agent, and workspace, then read the habits behind it: turns to completion, restarts on the same task, steering overridden by hand instead of written as a rule. Each habit carries its definition and one recommendation, worded as a rule the operator can adopt.
entries.qualifier: Read from the recorded turns and governed actions, not estimated.
entries.evidence: Product owner: demonstrate the per-operator review before this line runs. Show one habit with its definition and the recommendation it produces.
entries.notes: Candidate headline for the operations section, alongside the approved line. It pairs the two halves of the job, the agent and the person.

entries.title: Give each agent the tools and skills its work requires.
entries.long: Manage the tools and skills available to your workforce, then assign them through each agent's mandate. Pair the equipment with the authority to use it and the business context the agent is permitted to read.
entries.evidence: Engineering owner: show how an operator changes an assignment, which version an agent receives, and when the change takes effect. Do not promise centralized revocation or version pinning without demonstrated behavior.

entries.title: Manage the workforce from one console.
entries.long: See the agents enrolled in Oxagen, the mandates they work under, their open requests, and their recorded activity and spend. Answer an approval request, change an assignment, or adjust a budget from the operator console. Agents run in their supported environments, and Oxagen is the agent control plane that governs their work.
entries.qualifier: Use the hold and stop controls supported by each integration.
entries.evidence: Product owner: provide a launch walkthrough with identity, authority, tool and skill assignment, a recorded action, an ongoing agent, and a task with completion criteria. Document supported environments and control boundaries. Platform owner: demonstrate allow, deny, approval, missing-rule, observe-mode, and outage cases for each supported integration. Identify requests outside that boundary.
entries.notes: Describe what a control changes and when it takes effect.

entries.title: Define completion when the work has an endpoint.
entries.long: For a bounded task, set the checks and human decisions that determine completion before the agent starts. Oxagen locks those criteria into the run and records the results. For an ongoing responsibility, set the authority, budget, and review points that keep the work accountable over time.
entries.qualifier: A passing verdict means the specified checks held. Your team decides whether those checks are sufficient for the task.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: When checks fail, the record shows the reasons and whether the agent continued, waited for a person, or reached its retry limit.

entries.title: Identity, authority, and a record you can inspect.
entries.long: Review how agent identities map to your access controls, how Oxagen handles connection credentials, and what each governed action records. Inspect the supported deployment and integration boundaries before granting authority.
entries.cta_destination: The security page: identity mapping, credential handling for mediated connections, and the record of a governed action.
entries.evidence: Security owner: demonstrate provisioning, delegation, revocation, credential handling, and audit coverage. Before an attestation claim, verify the report type, entity, system scope, period, and access process against the actual report.
entries.notes: Any SOC 2 statement on this page follows rule-soc2-publication.

entries.title: Stella is an agent. Oxagen manages the workforce.
entries.evidence: Product owner: confirm the launch integration. Show Stella as one supported agent where that is accurate, and keep the platform story broad enough for other supported agents.
entries.notes: Shared branding does not establish shared proof mechanisms or identical capabilities.

entries.title: It does the work and proves it finished.
entries.evidence: Stella owner: the proof rule the tagline names is Stella's documented witness behavior.
entries.notes: Stella's social and manifest tagline, unchanged.

entries.title: Let the next reviewer check your work.
entries.short: Share the recorded evidence and evaluator versions behind a Witness verdict so another party can check the result.
entries.long: Witness ties its result to the requirement, the captured inputs, and the exact evaluators that checked them. Its signed record links to the evidence behind each verdict. A reviewer can recompute the result from those inputs and compare it with the recorded answer.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 26.

entries.title: Show that the change made the difference.
entries.short: Witness checks the target baseline and the pull request. Failing before and passing after earns a proven result for that requirement.
entries.long: Oxagen runs an independent witness against the pull request's target baseline and its proposed change in the same isolated environment. The required behavior must fail on the baseline and pass on the pull request. A check that passes both earns no proof of the change. The recorded flip shows which requirement the change satisfied, and proven covers that requirement only.
entries.qualifier: Proven covers the requirement the witness checks.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 21.

entries.title: Make room for judgment. Name who made it.
entries.short: Keep taste, tone, and other human decisions visible alongside the mechanical evidence.
entries.long: A schema can settle whether an output has the required fields. Brand tone still needs a reviewer. Witness routes those judgment calls to a person and records the signature separately. Anyone reading the result can see what the oracles established and what a human accepted.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 25.

entries.title: Keep the witness beyond the agent's reach.
entries.short: The agent works on the change. Witness runs separately, with its checks and environment hidden from the agent.
entries.long: Oxagen keeps the witness outside the agent's repository, tools, and working environment. By default, the agent receives only pass or fail. Changes that interfere with the witness's foundations are recorded as tampering. Your team controls any additional disclosure, and the record keeps what was shared.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 22.

entries.title: Models propose. Oracles decide.
entries.short: Turn a requirement into a check with a repeatable answer. Models can help write it. Recorded evidence determines the verdict.
entries.long: An oracle is a check with a defined answer. Compare an output with an expected value, validate a schema, check an invariant, or run a pinned command. Oxagen evaluates the captured evidence under fixed conditions. Missing evidence, an evaluator error, or a timeout produces a rejection with a reason.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 23.

entries.title: Tie the payment to the result.
entries.short: Define the outcome that releases funding and link the release to its Witness evidence.
entries.long: For outcome-funded work, set the required result in the witness record before the work begins. A qualifying Witness result triggers the funding release and links the metered outcome to its signed evidence. The payment record shows what earned it and which checks established the result.
entries.cta: Follow an outcome to its payment
entries.qualifier: For outcome-funded work.
entries.evidence: FinOps and engineering: provide a reproducible baseline, task set, model and rate versions, sample size, quality measure, and costs including retries and Oxagen fees. Report the distribution and exceptions, not only an average.
entries.notes: Launch card 28. A specific workflow. Not a claim that charges or provider costs disappear when work fails.

entries.title: Decide what would count before anyone builds it.
entries.short: Turn a requirement into inputs, expected behavior, limits, and executable examples your team can review.
entries.long: Witness Studio helps you express a requirement as something that can be checked. Define the starting state, the requested action, the expected result, and what must remain unchanged. Boundary conditions get examples that must be rejected. A requirement becomes ready when it includes an executable witness.
entries.evidence: Launch acceptance: demonstrate both an ongoing responsibility and a bounded task. Show check failure, retry limits, human review, and verdict recomputation for the latter. Do not imply that passing specified checks establishes universal correctness.
entries.notes: Launch card 24.

entries.title: See what your AI spend accomplished.
entries.short: Track spend on witness-proven runs separately from human-accepted work and work without proof.
entries.long: Oxagen connects run cost to its recorded outcome. See spend on runs with a witness flip, human-accepted results, and work that remains unproven. Compare cost per proven run across agents and over time. Each proven result links back to the requirement and the witness that flipped.
entries.qualifier: Proven means a witness flipped for a stated requirement.
entries.evidence: FinOps and engineering: provide a reproducible baseline, task set, model and rate versions, sample size, quality measure, and costs including retries and Oxagen fees. Report the distribution and exceptions, not only an average.
entries.notes: Launch card 27.
